messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: NEW INCIDENT auto-created: high-rate CUDA OOMs on streaming-decode -> node flaps and dropped streams. Severity P1. Pager: Emma.

Emma (oncall): I'm seeing a cluster of streaming pods failing with CUDA OOM during decode. Pods restart looped on gpu-pool-5 nodes, clients getting mid-stream disconnects.

Zeke (runtime): can you paste a representative error? also which build/revision?

Emma (oncall): build: streaming-decode@v7.4.2. Error sample from pod streaming-decode-7f8b: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3472000000 bytes
  at decode_loop.cu:emit_token
  at server/stream.cc:send_chunk
```
OOMs spike started ~08:22 UTC.

Priya (infra): affected nodes: gw-gpu-05, gw-gpu-07, gw-gpu-11. Node memory pressure high, some kubelet evictions. I'm seeing GPU memory 98% on gw-gpu-07.

Tom (support): Support metrics: ~150 customer streams had 5xx or abrupt closures in the last 12m. Notable customers hit: FinMap (prod), Draftly (prod). Both alerted.

Zeke (runtime): hypothesis: we pushed a change last night that relaxed server-side token enforcement in favor of client-declared limits. If clients omit max_tokens, runtime used an unbounded path that grows KV cache aggressively. Those long-run requests can consume multiple GBs.

Carlos (sre): immediate containment options: 1) enforce router-level max_tokens cap; 2) route high-risk keys to cpu-fallback; 3) scale up decode pool temporarily; 4) cordon worst nodes.

Emma (oncall): executing quick mitigations now: applying router cap to 2k tokens, adding header rewrite so missing x-max-tokens gets default 512, and returning 429 for any request that would exceed 4k. Patch applied to ingress config.

```
# router lua (pseudo)
if not req.get('x-max-tokens') then req.set_header('x-max-tokens','512') end
if tonumber(req.get('x-max-tokens')) > 2000 then req.set_header('x-max-tokens','2000'); req.set_header('x-token-truncated','true') end
```

Priya (infra): cordoned gw-gpu-07 and draining pods off gw-gpu-05. Scheduling a reboot for gw-gpu-11 after we stabilize. Also lowering stream pod resource limits (mem) to fail-fast instead of trying to allocate massive KV.

Zeke (runtime): pushed hotfix to runtime v7.4.3: early token-accounting check before KV cache expansion; if predicted mem > 1.5GB, runtime aborts with clear 413-like error and logs token_count/est_mem. Rolling out to canary now.

Tom (support): notified FinMap and Draftly with temporary mitigation steps and rollback ETA. Offering batch/async fallback for critical jobs.

Emma (oncall): after router caps + canary rollout, OOMs on canary nodes dropped from ~30/min to 2/min. Overall streaming success rose from 58% to 89%. Still seeing a small tail of failures on drained nodes.

Carlos (sre): moving high-error API keys to cpu-fallback pool for 1h to avoid repeat flaps. Will revert if stability holds.

Leah (product): need us to capture customer impact for AMR and PSR. Tom, please collate affected request counts and user-visible errors; I'll prepare comms.

Zeke (runtime): preliminary root cause narrows to three factors: 1) removal of a defensive server-side token cap in last deploy; 2) some clients sending very long-gen requests with no max_tokens; 3) KV-cache growth path in new decode code amplifies allocation per token. Concurrency of these requests led to >8GiB allocations on some nodes -> CUDA OOM -> kube restarts.

Emma (oncall): handoff: I'm assigning follow-up to Zeke for runtime fix and to Priya for infra remediation. I'll remain as incident lead until postmortem owner is defined.

Zeke (runtime): short-term actions: 1) keep router cap at 2k for 2 hours; 2) merge runtime v7.4.3 hotfix and rollout to 50% of decode fleet; 3) add a pre-serve token estimator to reject oversized streams.

Priya (infra): short-term infra: decommission gw-gpu-07 for a hardware recheck, reboot gw-gpu-11, run full mem-health diagnostics across gpu fleet, add alert when any single pod uses >70% GPU memory for >30s.

Tom (support): customer impact: two enterprise customers saw partial failures, logged as SLA incident. I've created INC-6227 and linked tickets. Tom to own customer comms with Leah.

Carlos (sre): medium-term: add integration test that simulates runaway generation at scale; add a routing circuit-breaker that enforces per-key token budgets and a throttling policy if thresholds exceeded.

Zeke (runtime): I'll also add unit tests and a synthetic workload that runs max-token stress under memory-constrained env to catch regressions in CI.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: MITIGATION APPLIED: router caps + runtime canary deployed + node drain/reboots in progress. Severity downgraded to P2.

Emma (oncall): handing off to Zeke for the post-incident work. Zeke, you're owning the postmortem and follow-ups. I'll continue monitoring dashboards for 1hr and then clear paging.

Zeke (runtime): acknowledged. I'll assemble timeline, affected customer list, and the fix PR. Targeting postmortem publish in 48h.

Priya (infra): leaving health checks running. Filing infra follow-up RFC for node-level GPU memory export and alerts.

Tom (support): updating customers: Draftly updated; FinMap accepted cpu-fallback for jobs and will retry later.

Leah (product): add postmortem action: review API guidance about max_tokens and consider requiring explicit max_tokens for streaming endpoints.

incident-bot: :information_source: next update scheduled in 30m. Archive artifacts stored at s3://incidents/2098765400/artifacts/

Emma (oncall): closing active paging for now; Zeke will take lead. Great quick work, team.

Zeke (runtime): final note: we should treat server-side defensive caps as critical safety nets. Removing them without end-to-end tests is risky. I'll include this in remediation tasks.
